attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, stated as his own view.

semantics.note: The normalisation keeps all three targets: what chatbots say or do, how they change, and how they treat users. It is a present-tense observation.

contract.note: The contract counts general FTC deception authority as meaningful chatbot regulation and rules it out as a trivial exception. Read in context, Marcus means rules aimed at chatbot content, changes over time and treatment of users. General law covering all businesses is not what he denied. That reading is stretched against him.

evidence.note: An openly identified copy of 2020 FTC blog guidance. It says misleading chatbot use could draw FTC Act action. It is guidance on general deception law and does not address chatbot changes or treatment of users.
An Italian regulator's action on Replika's data processing, wrongly labelled as a company disclosure. It is overseas data-protection enforcement, not US chatbot regulation.

reviews.rationale: The contradiction depends on treating general FTC deception law as chatbot regulation, which is unfair to the speaker. On a fair reading, the packet shows no US rules aimed at chatbot content, changes or treatment of users. It also does not show that no such rules existed; it only notes it found none. The packet does not settle it.

attribution.note: Marcus's own statement in his post.

semantics.note: Both parts are preserved: few understand how chatbots work, and many anthropomorphize them by attributing intelligence and emotion.

contract.note: Fair plain reading: it requires basic understanding and literal attribution, and imposes no numerical cutoffs.

evidence.note: A study of January 2023 Twitter discussion of AI. It does not measure how many people understand chatbots or attribute emotions to them.
A survey fielded April–May 2023, after the target period, about AI in general rather than chatbots. It cannot establish prevalence before February 22.

reviews.rationale: No item in the packet measures either part of the claim for the population and period. Both items are context only, so the outcome is unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post.

semantics.note: 'More and more people are using chatbots' becomes 'chatbot usage is increasing', which is faithful.

contract.note: Fair plain reading: a recent rise in adoption, measured with comparable unique-user figures for December 2022 to January 2023.

evidence.note: A Reuters report, citing a UBS study using Similarweb data, says ChatGPT's daily unique visitors more than doubled from December to January. That is a like-for-like user measure in the target period.

reviews.rationale: Independent audience measurement, reported by Reuters, shows daily unique visitors to the most prominent chatbot more than doubled from December 2022 to January 2023. The packet has no counterevidence. Supported.

attribution.note: Marcus's own statement in his post.

semantics.note: An existence claim that some people form real emotional attachments to chatbots. Faithful.

contract.note: Fair: it tests existence, not prevalence, and requires sincere affection or reliance from independent sources.

evidence.note: ABC interviews, published March 1, 2023, document Replika users' attachment and real hurt from changes around February 14. That falls within the period.

reviews.rationale: Independent interviews show users describing emotional attachment to Replika bots and real hurt from the February 2023 changes. That is enough for an existence claim. Supported.
